title: Nuclear charge and effective nuclear charge
topicTitle: Nuclear charge and effective nuclear charge
notes: **Nuclear charge.** The total positive charge of the nucleus is Ze, where Z is the atomic number and e the elementary charge; it is the nucleus's pull on the electron cloud.
**Shielding effect.** Inner-shell electrons repel outer electrons and cancel part of the nuclear pull; this screening is greatest in multi-electron atoms.
**Effective nuclear charge.** Zeff = Z − σ, where σ is the shielding constant; outer electrons feel this reduced attraction rather than the full nuclear charge.
**Trends across a period.** Electrons enter the same shell while Z rises, so shielding changes little and Zeff increases — atomic radius falls and ionisation enthalpy rises.
**Trends down a group.** Each new shell adds shielding that nearly cancels the added nuclear charge, so radius grows and ionisation enthalpy falls down the group.

universalFacts: Mass defect Δm = Z m_p + N m_n − M; binding energy BE = Δm c²; BE per nucleon peaks near Fe-56 (~8.8 MeV).
